# Example GitHub Secrets for deployment workflow
# Add these secrets to your repository at: Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > New repository secret
#
# Workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml):
#   verify   — branch push: build images, run unit tests and e2e locally, then push sha-<12>
#   publish  — after verify: move :latest (main) or a unique branch tag
#   deploy   — after verify on main: SSH, pull the tested sha tag, roll workloads
#
# sha-<12> is pushed only after unit tests and e2e pass, and only if that commit
# is still the branch tip. An older run does not move :latest or deploy.
# Branch tags are <sanitized-name>-<12 hex chars of the raw branch name>, so
# feature/foo and feature-foo do not overwrite each other, and the tag is never
# "latest".
# Images stay public after that push. The token is required to push.
# DOCKERHUB_USERNAME is the Docker Hub namespace (image prefix), not only the login.
#
# Optional repository variable (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables):
#   DEPLOY_PATH=/path/on/the/server/moneymaker_aws
# When unset, deploy uses $HOME/moneymaker_aws for the SSH user.

# Docker Hub Credentials
DOCKERHUB_USERNAME=prabuselvamnatarajan
DOCKERHUB_TOKEN=your_docker_hub_personal_access_token_here

# AWS SSH Deployment (only used on main branch)
HOST=your_aws_instance_ip_or_domain
USERNAME=ubuntu
PRIVATE_KEY=your_ssh_private_key_content_here
